speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO & Chairman (RTX)
quote: I'll start out with Dinesh Paliwal. Dinesh is -- please. He's our Lead Independent Director, former CEO and Chairman of HARMAN International and our Lead Director since the merger.
finding: With a combined chair and CEO, RTX has had a Lead Independent Director since the 2020 merger; in 2023 it was Dinesh Paliwal, a former Harman CEO with an operating background.

speaker: Thomas A. Kennedy, Executive Chairman of the Board
quote: Tracy Atkinson, retired Executive Vice President of State Street Corporation; Marshall Larsen, retired Chairman, President and CEO of Goodrich Corporation; George Oliver, Chairman and CEO, Johnson Controls International; Kelly Ortberg, retired Chairman, President and CEO, Rockwell Collins; Dr. Meghan O'Sullivan, Professor at the Harvard University Kennedy School; Dinesh Paliwal, retired Chairman, President and CEO, Harman International, who serves as our Independent Lead Director; Ellen Pawlikowski, retired General, United States Air Force and former Commander, Air Force Materiel Command; Denise Ramos, retired CEO and President, ITT; Fredric Reynolds, retired Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, CBS Corporation; Brian Rogers, retired Chairman, T. Rowe Price Group; James Winnefeld, retired Admiral, United States Navy and former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff; Robert Work, retired Deputy Secretary of Defense, U.S. Department of Defense; and our newest director, Dr. Bernard Harris, CEO of Vesalius Ventures
finding: The chair's own introduction gives the backgrounds of eight of the ten directors elected in 2026 (PG-0041): Atkinson (State Street), Oliver (Johnson Controls CEO), Pawlikowski (USAF Materiel Command), Ramos (ITT CEO), Reynolds (CBS CFO), Rogers (T. Rowe Price chairman), Work (Deputy Secretary of Defense) and Harris (astronaut, venture CEO). Calio and Caret joined later; both are on the February 2025 director list (PG-0062).

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, President & CEO (UTC)
quote: We welcome Mr. Fred Reynolds joining us. Fred's a retired CFO at CBS. He's also on the Mondelez board. We welcome Fred, great financial mind. We also welcome Brian Rogers from T. Rowe Price onto the board. Again, people focused on what investors, what you guys are focused on.
finding: Two directors still on the board in 2026, including today's Lead Independent Director (Reynolds), were brought in as investor-minded financial voices.

speaker: Greg Hayes, CEO (RTX)
quote: We have a very strong Board of Directors. If you think about the Board, we've got great commercial aero experience between Marshall Larsen, Kelly Ortberg, Denise Ramos and George Oliver, all people with long service in commercial aerospace markets. On the defense side, Admiral Sandy Winnefeld, former Vice Chair of the Joint Chiefs; Ellen Pawlikowski; Bob Work; Meghan O'Sullivan; and Bernard Harris, again solid defense credentials.
finding: In 2021 the board mixed commercial-aerospace operators (Larsen, Ortberg, Ramos, Oliver) with defence figures. Larsen and Ortberg are no longer on the February 2025 director list (PG-0062), and Winnefeld, still on it, is not on the 2026 slate (PG-0041): the commercial-aerospace operating bench has thinned.

speaker: Greg Hayes, CEO (RTX)
quote: this governance, the focus is on one thing, that is making sure that we have the right talent and the right leadership for the business over the long haul. ... The idea of succession and talent development, not a Board meeting goes by where we don't discuss that.
finding: Management describes the board's main governance focus as leadership for the long haul, with succession on the agenda of every board meeting.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman, CEO & President (UTC)
quote: Tom will assume the role of Executive Chairman of the Board for 2 years following the completion of the merger, and I'll assume the role of CEO of the formation and succeed Tom as Chairman of the Board after his 2-year tenure. In terms of the Board's composition, we'll have 15 members, 8 from UTC and 7 from Raytheon.
finding: The RTX board was built by merger agreement: 15 seats split 8 UTC and 7 Raytheon, with a pre-agreed path to a combined chair and CEO (Hayes) after two years.

speaker: Thomas A. Kennedy, Executive Chairman of the Board
quote: I'll be retiring as Executive Chairman of the Board of Directors for Raytheon Technologies, a role I assumed upon the close of the merger between Raytheon Company and United Technologies last April. I am pleased that Greg Hayes will be taking on the role of Chairman and CEO as of June 1, when I will transition out of my role.
finding: The board recombined the chair and CEO roles from June 2021, about ten months before the end of the two-year Executive Chairman term agreed at the merger (PG-0006); RTX's default model is a combined chair and CEO with a lead independent director.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, President, CEO & Director
quote: strength allowed us to confirm our commitment to return significant capital to shareowners. Making good on that promise, our Board this morning approved a 7% increase in our quarterly dividend.
finding: Coming out of the COVID year the board's first visible act was a 7% dividend increase: the board treats dividend growth as a promise to keep.

speaker: Michael Barbera, Inspector of Election
quote: each of the director nominees has been elected to the Board with the majority of the votes cast. With regard to the advisory vote to approve the compensation of the senior executives named in the proxy statement, the proposal was approved, having received 91% of the votes in favor.
finding: Shareholders back the board and its pay design by large majorities (91% say-on-pay in 2021). No controlling or state shareholder appears in our evidence (inference from absence).

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO
quote: the return of the $18 billion to $20 billion that we outlined last June will more likely take place over a 4-year versus a 3-year time frame. We also remain committed to the dividend which our Board approved last week. And we have sufficient cash and liquidity to maintain a competitive dividend even in this very difficult environment.
finding: At the bottom of COVID the board stretched the capital-return timetable but approved the dividend unchanged: it flexes buybacks and timing, never the dividend.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, President, CEO & Director
quote: And I think everybody agreed we have got the financial flexibility to continue to pay the current dividend and to grow the dividend as earnings recover. So that is our commitment is the dividend will remain in place, I mean, unless something completely unforeseen happens.
finding: The board's COVID dividend decision rested on downside stress scenarios shown to it in April 2020 (P-0423); the board's risk test is liquidity under a stress case, and the dividend is the last thing to give.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, President, CEO & Director
quote: Kennedy and myself have agreed to a 20% pay reduction for the remainder of the year. The Raytheon Technologies Board of Directors will take up this issue of their own compensation later today, and we will report on that. Their compensation is strictly related to an annual stipend. There are no bonuses and therefore nothing to cut.
finding: Directors are paid a fixed annual retainer with no bonus, so their own pay is not tied to short-term results; in COVID the chair and CEO took 20% pay cuts.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman, CEO & President (UTC)
quote: So look, time will tell, right, whether or not we've made a good deal. I think, we all believe, the Board believes this is the right thing to do for shareowners over the long term.
finding: The board approved the Raytheon merger, a portfolio-defining bet, on a long-term value argument, accepting near-term doubt about the price.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: the board's decision to pursue a separation of the existing UTC portfolio is a pivotal moment in our history and follows a more than a yearlong comprehensive evaluation of the portfolio in which we considered a wide range of options.
finding: The board took the UTC break-up decision only after a year-long review of a wide range of options: big structural moves are slow and evidence-heavy.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: It's one of the key questions that the board asked management as we were going through this process, say, were there investments that Carrier or Otis did not make over the last decade that they would have made as an independent company? And I think obviously, the answer to that is yes. I think the fact that Otis lost a lot of market share over the last decade in pursuit of higher margins was something that Otis would not have done as a stand-alone business.
finding: The board asked whether the conglomerate had under-invested for margin; it read share lost 'in pursuit of higher margins' as a cost. Evidence of a long-term, share-and-investment lens on the board.

speaker: Akhil Johri, Executive VP & CFO (UTC)
quote: we have committed to the board to have in-depth discussions about all the questions that, I'm sure, you and the board members would have about it's a big decision, we need to make sure we provide them with all the data, with all the thinking around this
finding: For a big decision the board expects in-depth sessions with all the data and the reasoning; management commits to that before asking for a decision.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: as we sit here today, we don't have to do anything. We've got great businesses. We've got great growth prospects. The question that the board has to answer, that we have to answer is what is the best way to create additional long-term shareowner value.
finding: The board frames its test as long-term shareowner value, and is comfortable that doing nothing is an option.

speaker: Akhil Johri, Executive VP & CFO (UTC)
quote: The stock compensation plan will still be reliant on the UTX performance and the ROIC and the other metrics we have.
finding: Long-term (stock) incentives were tied to company-wide performance including ROIC, while near-term cash incentives were moved to business-unit results.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, President & CEO (UTC)
quote: one of the changes that we're making at UTC around our incentive plans is we're actually introducing an ROIC metric. So for the first time, you will see next year in our long-term comp incentives the ROIC metric. Because quite frankly, capital is not free and we need to measure it, and we need to get people focused on it. ... This is a 3-year long-term plan, that will help.
finding: From 2016 the long-term incentive plan carries a 3-year ROIC metric: capital discipline is written into pay, which penalises capital-heavy launches that do not earn their return within the plan window.

speaker: Akhil Johri, Executive VP & CFO (UTC)
quote: our long-term incentive goal became 6% as opposed to 10% we have traditionally had. Look, the reality, Myles, is that with all the investments we have made and the pressures that are coming on the earnings as a result of that near term ... Our long-term incentive plans, which was the '14 to '16 plan is likely to pay out 0 on the EPS side, right? ... And it's -- and obviously, the comp committee looks at all that.
finding: By 2016 the long-term incentive EPS growth goal had been set at 6% instead of the traditional 10% (the 2015-17 plan), because the engine investments (R&D and negative engine margin) were weighing on near-term earnings; the CFO says the compensation committee 'looks at all that' and that pay must still retain talent. The board reset pay goals rather than the investment (the motive is inference).

speaker: Akhil Johri, Executive VP & CFO (UTC)
quote: If there was one transaction in the world for which I was willing to, and I think our board and Greg were willing to take a little hit, right, on our returns expectations, it is Rockwell.
finding: The board will accept a return below its usual hurdle (IRR above 10%, P-0272) only for a rare strategic aerospace asset; the exception proves the rule.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: the Rockwell deal today, here it is 9 months later, looks a heck of a lot better than the -- even the deal that we approved with the board last summer. And I think, again, it is the long-term nature of the aerospace business and what we see today going forward that is going to make Rockwell a great, great addition to UTC.
finding: The board approved the $30bn Rockwell Collins purchase (P-0320) in 2017 on the long-term nature of aerospace: it will take big, long-cycle aerospace bets when the strategic case is strong.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: We had a Board of Directors meeting here this week, and we took them out to the test cell. And there's nothing like seeing the GTF on a test stand and then, 10 minutes later, seeing a JSF on a test stand.
finding: The board meets at Pratt & Whitney sites and sees the engines on test; it has direct exposure to the GTF programme.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (UTC)
quote: If GTF costs are higher, or reef [ph] costs are higher, that gets reflected. So it's a dynamic model. We're constantly looking at. We share this with the board a couple of times a year. Just to give people confidence, this is where we think we need to be.
finding: The board sees the intrinsic-value model (8% cost of capital, product-line level, GTF costs included; P-1163) a couple of times a year: it judges capital calls against value per share.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, Chairman & CEO (RTX)
quote: And talking to the Board, we just felt that it was time to -- as we're thinking about succession planning, leadership development, this was a good time to get Chris a broader scope of responsibilities.
finding: The board groomed Chris Calio (ex-Pratt & Whitney president) as successor from 2022 by making him COO over all four businesses.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO & Chairman (RTX)
quote: Chris' appointment is the result of a very deliberate and thoughtful succession planning process conducted by our Board of Directors over the past 3 years. While I'm going to remain in my role as Executive Chairman, Chris will be taking the reins of the company.
finding: The board ran a three-year succession process and chose an insider from Pratt & Whitney as CEO (May 2024), keeping Hayes as Executive Chairman for continuity.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO & Chairman (RTX)
quote: I can't think of a better leader than Chris to lead RTX for the next decade or so. You should all know that Chris has the full support of the Board, but not just the Board, the entire senior leadership team and the entire organization.
finding: The board publicly backs Calio as a decade-long CEO: a stable, supportive relationship with management.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO & Chairman (RTX)
quote: Given the fundamental strength of the company and growth opportunities ahead, our Board recently approved an $11 billion authority to repurchase RTX shares. This includes $10 billion through an ASR program to help capture some of that value more immediately.
finding: Three months into the powder-metal crisis the board approved an $11bn buyback authority, $10bn of it as an immediate ASR.

speaker: Gregory J. Hayes, CEO & Chairman (RTX)
quote: I would tell you, we had a fulsome discussion with the Board about the timing of the ASR. ... This is another $10 billion at what I believe to be a significant discount to intrinsic value. And this is the time to buy.
finding: The board debated the timing and still chose a debt-funded $10bn buyback in the middle of the GTF recall: it accepted balance-sheet risk (rating outlook to negative, P-1554) to buy stock it judged undervalued.

speaker: Christopher T. Calio, Chairman & CEO
quote: And we remain committed to a long-term capital return policy that includes growing our dividend and returning excess capital to shareowners.
finding: Under Calio as chair, the board's standing policy is a growing dividend plus return of excess capital, alongside deleveraging (P-0686).

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: Decisions with respect to dividends and share repurchases are subject to the discretion of our Board of Directors and are based on a variety of factors. Important factors that could cause us to discontinue, limit, suspend, increase, or delay our quarterly cash dividends or share repurchases include market conditions, the price of our common stock, the nature and timing of other investment opportunities, changes in our business strategy, the terms of our financing arrangements
finding: Dividends and buybacks are reserved to the board, which weighs them against other investment opportunities and financing terms.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: Our Corporate Governance Guidelines and the charters of our Board of Directors' Audit Committee, Finance Committee, Governance and Public Policy Committee, Human Capital and Compensation Committee, and Special Activities Committee are available on our website
finding: RTX has five standing board committees: Audit, Finance, Governance and Public Policy, Human Capital and Compensation, and Special Activities. There is no dedicated safety or technology committee.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: Our Board of Directors has primary oversight responsibility for enterprise cybersecurity risks. The Special Activities Committee of the Board supports the Board in oversight of classified business cybersecurity, including with respect to Company internal information and operational technology systems. The Audit Committee also considers enterprise cybersecurity risks in connection with its financial and compliance risk oversight role.
finding: Risk oversight is split between the full board, the Special Activities Committee (classified business) and the Audit Committee (financial and compliance risk).

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: The top ERM risks are compiled annually and shared with the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors as well as the full Board of Directors. In addition, Internal Audit incorporates these risks into its continuous risk assessment process
finding: The board reviews the top enterprise risks once a year through the Audit Committee and in full session; enterprise risk is a standing board process.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: On October 21, 2023, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for up to $11 billion of our common stock, replacing the previous program announced on December 12, 2022. Under the 2023 program, shares may be purchased on the open market, in privately negotiated transactions, under accelerated share repurchase programs
finding: The board's $11bn authorisation of 21 October 2023 (during the powder-metal recall) is still the standing authority at end-2024.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: On December 7, 2020, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for up to $5 billion of our common stock, replacing the previous program announced on October 14, 2015.
finding: In December 2020, with commercial aerospace still depressed, the board authorised a new $5bn buyback: returns restart as soon as liquidity allows.

speaker: United Technologies Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: On October 14, 2015, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for up to $12 billion of our common stock.
finding: During the GTF development and ramp the UTC board authorised a $12bn buyback programme (2015), funding returns and the engine at the same time.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: On January 31, 2025, the Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.63 per share payable March 20, 2025 to shareowners of record at the close of business on February 21, 2025.
finding: The board declares each quarterly dividend. In January 2025 it held the dividend at $0.63, the level set in 2024; the same page shows dividends paid per share of $2.16 (2022), $2.32 (2023) and $2.48 (2024), so the per-share dividend rose each year through the powder-metal charge. The 2025 increase came later (8% in July 2025, P-0677).

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: multiple shareholder derivative lawsuits were filed against current and former officers and directors of the Company, all of which have now been consolidated into a single action which is pending in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware. The operative complaint in the consolidated action alleges that the defendants caused the Company to make materially false and misleading statements relating to Pratt & Whitney's GTF engines, and failed to maintain an adequate system of oversight
finding: The GTF powder-metal crisis put the directors themselves in the dock: shareholders allege a failure of board oversight of P&W's engines. This raises the board's sensitivity to engine-quality and disclosure risk.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: on October 15, 2024, Raytheon Company entered into a deferred prosecution agreement (DPA) (DPA-1) with the DOJ and on October 16, 2024, the Company became subject to an administrative order issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission ... Under DPA-1, DPA-2, and the SEC Administrative Order, Raytheon Company and the Company are required, among other things, to retain an independent compliance monitor satisfactory to the DOJ and the SEC (for a term ending three years from the date on which the monitor is engaged)
finding: Since October 2024 RTX operates under deferred prosecution agreements and an independent compliance monitor for three years; the board's oversight agenda is heavy with compliance remediation.

speaker: RTX Corporation (Form 10-K)
quote: 24 Powers of Attorney of Tracy A. Atkinson, Leanne G. Caret, Bernard A. Harris, Jr., Gregory J. Hayes, George R. Oliver, Ellen M. Pawlikowski, Denise L. Ramos, Fredric G. Reynolds, Brian C. Rogers, James A. Winnefeld, Jr. and Robert O. Work.
finding: As of the FY2024 10-K (signed 3 February 2025) the board had twelve members: these eleven plus Calio, who signs as CEO; Hayes signs as Executive Chairman (signature page). Larsen, Ortberg and Paliwal are gone; Winnefeld and Hayes are still directors. This is the latest board list in the repo's own sources.
